records.description: Selective Permeability in Protocellular Boundaries denotes the admissible property-level arising in which primitive membrane-like boundary structures allow differential passage of molecules and ions, thereby establishing controlled internal chemical conditions without requiring fully developed transport machinery. Within Level 3 this arising is not a single diffusion event or a boundary object considered in isolation, but a functional property of protocellular enclosure through which boundary composition, thickness, packing state, and physicochemical characteristics bias partitioning, retention, and transboundary exchange. The arising establishes a primitive control capability that allows some species to enter or leave more readily than others, enabling retention of polymers and reactive intermediates while still permitting nutrient influx and waste efflux. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a property because the ontological unit is the enduring exchange-selectivity capability of the protocellular boundary rather than the individual transport events through which it is manifested. This arising provides the structural basis for stabilization of distinct internal composition, maintenance of reaction-supporting concentration differences, and support of sustained proto-metabolic organization within bounded chemical systems.
records.name: Selective Permeability in Protocellular Boundaries
records.shortDescription: Property-level differential permeability of primitive boundaries that regulates exchange and stabilizes distinct internal chemical conditions.
records.summary: Property-level differential permeability of primitive boundaries that regulates exchange and stabilizes distinct internal chemical conditions.

records.description: Encapsulation of Polymers and Catalysts in Protocells denotes the admissible process-level arising in which bounded compartments such as vesicles, coacervate droplets, or mixed protocellular boundary structures capture and retain informational polymers, catalysts, and related macromolecular components. Within Level 3 this arising is not merely the existence of a compartment object or the passive presence of internal molecules, but the dynamic confinement regime through which enclosure, retention, reduced dilution, enhanced proximity, and controlled exchange jointly create localized biochemical microenvironments. The arising establishes a condition in which templates and catalysts become co-localized within bounded internal space, allowing reaction coupling, selective amplification, and network persistence to become more stable than in unconfined media. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the confinement-and-retention regime itself rather than the protocell object or the encapsulated molecules considered independently. This arising provides the structural basis for localized reaction intensification, persistence of functional polymers, early genotype-phenotype coupling, and the emergence of compartment-supported biochemical organization.
records.name: Encapsulation of Polymers and Catalysts in Protocells
records.shortDescription: Process-level confinement of functional polymers and catalysts within primitive compartments, enabling localized reaction networks and stabilized biochemical coupling.
records.summary: Process-level confinement of functional polymers and catalysts within primitive compartments, enabling localized reaction networks and stabilized biochemical coupling.

records.description: Coupled Growth–Division Cycles of Protocellular Compartments denote a hypothesized process-level regime in which primitive compartments undergo recurrent expansion through material uptake and internal synthesis, followed by division through mechanical instability, curvature stress, or environmentally induced fission. Within Level 3 this arising is not merely the existence of vesicles or isolated fission events, but a coupled life-cycle regime through which boundary growth, internal chemical activity, resource access, and instability thresholds become dynamically linked. The arising establishes a reproducible compartmental cycle in which expansion and partitioning are not fully random but are conditioned by material availability, membrane state, and internal composition. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the recurrent growth-division regime itself rather than the compartment object or the inherited contents considered independently. This arising provides the structural basis for non-random inheritance of internal constituents, sustained protocellular populations, and the emergence of preselection dynamics at the level of bounded chemical compartments.
records.name: Coupled Growth–Division Cycles of Protocellular Compartments
records.shortDescription: Hypothesized process-level coupling of protocellular growth and division-like recurrence through material uptake, boundary expansion, and mechanically or chemically induced fission.
records.summary: Hypothesized process-level coupling of protocellular growth and division-like recurrence through material uptake, boundary expansion, and mechanically or chemically induced fission.

records.description: Chemiosmotic Energy Transduction in Proto-Membranes denotes the admissible property-level arising in which electrochemical gradients across primitive boundary structures become usable sources of free-energy coupling for internal biochemical organization. Within Level 3 this arising is not a single gradient-dissipation event or a membrane object alone, but a protocellular energetic property through which proton or ion gradients act as persistent non-equilibrium constraints that bias reaction directions, support coupling of otherwise unfavorable steps, and stabilize network operation prior to fully developed respiratory or transport machinery. The arising establishes a directional energetic relation between boundary-maintained gradients and interior chemical transformation, allowing boundary properties to participate directly in the regulation of internal biochemical dynamics. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a property because the ontological unit is the enduring gradient-coupling capability of the proto-membrane system rather than the individual flux events through which it is expressed. This arising provides the structural basis for primitive chemiosmotic biasing, non-equilibrium energetic support of internal reaction networks, and early boundary-mediated energy transduction in protocellular organization.
records.name: Chemiosmotic Energy Transduction in Proto-Membranes
records.shortDescription: Property-level use of electrochemical gradients across primitive boundaries to bias internal reactions and sustain non-equilibrium energetic coupling.
records.summary: Property-level use of electrochemical gradients across primitive boundaries to bias internal reactions and sustain non-equilibrium energetic coupling.

records.description: Protocellular Selection as a Population-Level Effect denotes the admissible effect-level arising in which heterogeneous protocellular compartments exhibit differential persistence, growth, and division-like recurrence under shared environmental constraints, causing some compartment types to increase in relative frequency over time. Within Level 3 this arising is not a single protocell object or one internal chemical process, but an ensemble-level outcome generated when differences in boundary maintenance, internal catalytic organization, encapsulated composition, and resource coupling are filtered across a population. The arising establishes a transition from isolated compartmental chemistry to population-level configurational sorting, where physicochemical performance differentials produce systematic shifts in distribution even in the absence of fully developed genetic inheritance. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as an effect because the ontological unit is the aggregate population-level consequence of many interacting protocellular trajectories rather than any individual compartment or specific local mechanism. This arising provides the structural basis for early selection-like dynamics, enrichment of more persistent compartment types, and the emergence of ensemble-level filtering prior to mature biological evolutionary regimes.
records.name: Protocellular Selection as a Population-Level Effect
records.shortDescription: Effect-level differential persistence and frequency change among protocellular compartments arising from variation in chemistry, stability, and growth-division performance.
records.summary: Effect-level differential persistence and frequency change among protocellular compartments arising from variation in chemistry, stability, and growth-division performance.

records.description: Photopigment Photon Absorption and Isomerization denotes the admissible process-level arising in which a photopigment molecule absorbs a photon and undergoes a rapid quantized conformational change that converts electromagnetic input into a discrete chemical state difference. Within Level 3 this arising is not merely the existence of a photopigment object, but the initiating photochemical transduction regime through which an embedded chromophore enters an excited state and proceeds through ultrafast isomerization within a structured protein environment. The arising establishes the first biochemical signal-bearing state change that can be amplified, regulated, and integrated by downstream biochemical networks. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the photon-triggered conversion event itself rather than the photopigment molecule considered independently. This arising provides the structural basis for phototransduction onset and marks the boundary at which physical photon interaction becomes chemically usable biochemical signaling without presupposing higher sensory or neural organization.
records.name: Photopigment Photon Absorption and Isomerization
records.shortDescription: Process-level primary photochemical conversion of absorbed photon energy into a localized chemical state change in a photopigment molecule.
records.summary: Process-level primary photochemical conversion of absorbed photon energy into a localized chemical state change in a photopigment molecule.

records.description: Cooperativity in Proteins and Complexes denotes the admissible property-level arising in which multiple binding sites, catalytic regions, or structural subunits within a protein or protein assembly become energetically and conformationally coupled so that local state changes systematically alter the response properties of other sites. Within Level 3 this arising is not an independent process of transformation or a separate macromolecular object, but a distributed functional property of a structured molecular system whose internal coupling architecture enables coordinated non-linear behavior. The arising establishes long-range response integration across the macromolecule or complex, allowing binding, catalysis, or conformational shifts at one location to reshape the accessibility, affinity, or activity of others. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a property because the ontological unit is a collective functional disposition of the protein or assembly rather than a discrete event or bounded object. This arising provides the structural basis for sensitivity amplification, switch-like response, threshold behavior, allosteric coordination, and integrated biochemical regulation across coupled molecular sites.
records.name: Cooperativity in Proteins and Complexes
records.shortDescription: Property-level collective coupling of sites or subunits in proteins and assemblies that produces coordinated non-linear functional response.
records.summary: Property-level collective coupling of sites or subunits in proteins and assemblies that produces coordinated non-linear functional response.

records.description: DNA-Directed RNA Synthesis denotes the admissible process-level arising in which an RNA polymerase reads a DNA template strand and synthesizes complementary RNA from nucleoside triphosphates, so that stored sequence becomes RNA products that act as messages, adaptors, catalysts and regulators. Within Level 3 this arising is not the copying of the genome itself, nor the decoding of messages into polypeptides, but the expression-side copying regime through which DNA sequence constraints are converted into operational RNA molecules whose base composition and sequence follow the template. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the template-directed RNA-synthesis regime rather than the DNA template, the polymerase or the RNA products considered independently. This arising provides the biochemical basis for gene expression, the production of messenger, transfer, ribosomal and regulatory RNAs, and the directional flow of sequence information from DNA to RNA.
records.name: DNA-Directed RNA Synthesis (Transcription)
records.shortDescription: Process-level polymerase-catalysed synthesis of RNA complementary to a DNA template strand, converting stored sequence into RNA products.
records.summary: Process-level polymerase-catalysed synthesis of RNA complementary to a DNA template strand, converting stored sequence into RNA products.

records.description: The Genetic Code denotes the admissible pattern-level arising of a reproducible mapping between nucleotide triplets (codons) and amino acids, together with start and stop signals. The mapping is implemented by transfer RNA adaptors whose anticodons pair with codons and by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases that load each transfer RNA with its cognate amino acid. Within Level 3 this arising is not the translation process that reads messages, nor the base-pairing rules it employs, but the assignment rule itself that makes a nucleic-acid sequence an instruction for a protein sequence. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a pattern because the ontological unit is the reproducible relational mapping between two molecular alphabets rather than any single adaptor, enzyme or message. This arising provides the structural basis for coded protein synthesis, the heritable correspondence between genes and proteins, and the informational coupling of nucleic-acid and protein domains of biochemical organization.
records.name: Genetic Code: Codon–Amino-Acid Assignment

records.shortDescription: Pattern-level reproducible assignment of nucleotide triplets to amino acids and stop signals, implemented by tRNA adaptors and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases.

records.description: Enzymatic Complex denotes the admissible object-level formation of a persistent multi-component biochemical assembly in which multiple enzymes and associated molecular components are structurally integrated into a single coordinated catalytic architecture. Within Level 3 this arising consists of a bounded higher-order molecular object whose internal spatial organization, interface stability, catalytic complementarity, and coupling relations enable collective reaction performance beyond isolated enzyme action. The assembly is not merely a sequence of related catalytic processes, but an identifiable structured object that maintains coordinated function through physical association of its constituents. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as an object because the ontological unit is the stable integrated multienzyme assembly itself rather than the catalytic events occurring within it or the regulatory properties it may exhibit. This arising establishes the structural basis for substrate channeling, synchronized reaction sequencing, reduction of diffusive loss, local pathway integration, and higher-order biochemical coordination within organized molecular systems.
records.name: Enzymatic Complex
records.shortDescription: Object-level multi-enzyme assembly enabling coordinated catalysis, substrate channeling, and integrated biochemical regulation.
records.summary: Object-level multi-enzyme assembly enabling coordinated catalysis, substrate channeling, and integrated biochemical regulation.

records.description: RNA Folding and Catalytic Activity denotes the admissible process-level arising in which a single-stranded RNA polymer enters a constrained three-dimensional conformational regime capable of catalytic and regulatory biochemical function. Within Level 3 this arising is not merely the existence of an RNA molecule, but the dynamic structural organization through which intramolecular base pairing, stacking interactions, tertiary contacts, solvent coupling, and ion-mediated stabilization produce active geometries and functionally determinate conformational states. The arising establishes protein-independent biochemical capability by enabling catalysis, ligand recognition, conformational switching, and regulation directly from nucleic acid organization. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the folding-and-activation regime itself rather than the RNA object considered apart from its functional conformational dynamics. This arising provides a structural bridge from nucleic acid polymer composition to direct biochemical functionality and supports RNA-centered scenarios of molecular regulation, catalysis, and early biochemical organization.
records.name: RNA Folding and Catalytic Activity
records.shortDescription: Process-level arising of functional RNA conformations enabling catalysis and regulatory action through nucleic-acid-intrinsic structural organization.
records.summary: Process-level arising of functional RNA conformations enabling catalysis and regulatory action through nucleic-acid-intrinsic structural organization.

records.description: Ribozymes denote the admissible object-level formation of persistent RNA-based catalytic units whose folded three-dimensional nucleic-acid structures realize specific biochemical reaction capability. Within Level 3 this arising consists of identifiable catalytic RNA objects that maintain functional identity through sequence-dependent structural stabilization, tertiary organization, and ion-supported active conformations. These are not merely transient catalytic processes, but bounded molecular units in which informational substrate and catalytic function coexist within the same RNA carrier. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as an object because the ontological unit is the stabilized catalytic RNA entity itself rather than the folding process that generates it or the catalytic property abstracted from its carrier. This arising establishes a biochemical regime in which catalysis, information-bearing sequence structure, and regulatory potential are integrated within a single molecular substrate, supporting RNA-mediated metabolism, control, and early biochemical organization.
records.name: Ribozymes
records.shortDescription: Object-level RNA catalytic units whose folded nucleic-acid structures realize stable and specific biochemical reaction capability.
records.summary: Object-level RNA catalytic units whose folded nucleic-acid structures realize stable and specific biochemical reaction capability.

records.description: Self-Organization of Viral Capsids denotes the admissible process-level arising in which viral structural subunits assemble into ordered capsid shells through internally determined interaction compatibilities, geometric constraints, and free-energy-guided biochemical self-organization. Within Level 3 this arising is not the capsid object itself, but the assembly regime through which local interface rules, subunit matching, cooperative stabilization, and closure-compatible geometry produce a reproducible global shell architecture without external macroscopic guidance. The arising establishes a transition from dispersed molecular components to integrated protective structural organization, demonstrating how higher-order ordered architectures can be realized through constrained multicomponent assembly dynamics. Within SOMA this phenomenon is classified as a process because the ontological unit is the assembly trajectory and structural closure regime itself rather than the completed capsid object considered independently. This arising provides the structural basis for robust viral shell formation, symmetry-constrained packaging architectures, and the emergence of information-bearing protective enclosures from relatively simple molecular components.
records.name: Self-Organization of Viral Capsids
records.shortDescription: Process-level spontaneous assembly of viral structural subunits into ordered capsid architectures through constrained biochemical self-organization.
records.summary: Process-level spontaneous assembly of viral structural subunits into ordered capsid architectures through constrained biochemical self-organization.

records.description: Prokaryotic Cell Organization denotes the admissible object-level formation of a prokaryotic cell as a bounded, self-maintaining biochemical unit with integrated metabolism, energy transduction, and template-based information processing. Within Level 4 this arising functions as a distinct cellular object because the prokaryotic cell possesses persistent structural identity across exchange, growth, and division cycles, while maintaining an internal regime differentiated from the external environment. Its organization couples membrane-bounded containment, selective exchange, autocatalytic production, bioenergetic throughput, replication, transcription, translation, and physicochemical stabilization into a single viable cellular architecture. This arising establishes the minimal autonomous cellular object regime in which heredity, catalytic renewal, regulated resource use, and repeatable division become structurally admissible under suitable environmental conditions.
records.name: Prokaryotic Cell Organization
records.shortDescription: Autonomous object-level cellular organization in which boundary maintenance, metabolism, and information processing are integrated within a persistent prokaryotic cell.
records.summary: Autonomous object-level cellular organization in which boundary maintenance, metabolism, and information processing are integrated within a persistent prokaryotic cell.

records.description: Eukaryotic Cell Compartmentalization denotes the admissible object-level organization of a eukaryotic cell in which internal membrane-bound compartments establish persistent specialized subdomains within a single cellular unit. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as an object because the compartmentalized eukaryotic cell possesses stable internal architectural identity defined by enduring organelle structure, regulated exchange, and coordinated intracellular division of functional domains. Internal membranes act as causal separators that localize reactions, constrain diffusion, protect information-processing environments, support targeted assembly, and enable parallel biochemical regimes that would otherwise interfere within an undifferentiated cytoplasmic space. This arising restructures intracellular causality by introducing persistent organelle-level boundaries that organize flows of matter, energy, and information across nucleus, endomembrane system, mitochondria, and related compartments, thereby enabling higher-resolution regulation, functional specialization, and expanded cellular complexity.
records.name: Eukaryotic Cell Compartmentalization
records.shortDescription: Object-level intracellular organization in which stable membrane-bound compartments create specialized internal domains for separated and coordinated cellular functions.
records.summary: Object-level intracellular organization in which stable membrane-bound compartments create specialized internal domains for separated and coordinated cellular functions.

records.description: DNA Repair Mechanisms and Genome Stability denote the admissible process-level organization in which molecular repair pathways, regulatory signaling, and controlled gene expression are integrated into a coordinated cellular regime that preserves the integrity of genetic information over time. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing detection of DNA damage, replication errors, and chemical modifications, the selection and activation of appropriate repair pathways, and the coordination of repair with replication, transcription, checkpoint control, and cell-fate responses. Genome stability here is maintained through regulated cellular operations rather than isolated molecular events, including repair, tolerance, arrest, and when necessary transition toward programmed cell death. This arising establishes the cellular-scale maintenance regime through which genetic material remains sufficiently stable for continued viability, inheritance, and controlled function.
records.name: DNA Repair Mechanisms and Genome Stability
records.shortDescription: Process-level cellular regime detecting, repairing, and preserving genome integrity under ongoing damage and replication stress.
records.summary: Process-level cellular regime detecting, repairing, and preserving genome integrity under ongoing damage and replication stress.

records.description: Intracellular Transport and Cytoskeletal Systems denote the admissible process-level organization in which structural polymers, motor proteins, and regulatory signaling are integrated into a coordinated intracellular framework for spatial organization and directed transport. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing assembly, remodeling, routing, and force-coupled movement of vesicles, organelles, macromolecular complexes, and signaling components within the bounded cellular space. The cytoskeletal system functions both as a mechanical scaffold and as a directional transport infrastructure, enabling targeted redistribution of cellular contents, spatial differentiation of functional zones, and dynamic reconfiguration during growth, polarization, and division. This arising establishes the regulated cellular transport regime through which internal positioning, cargo delivery, and structural coordination become reliably admissible.
records.name: Intracellular Transport and Cytoskeletal Systems
records.shortDescription: Process-level organization of directed intracellular transport through cytoskeletal structures, motor activity, and regulated spatial routing.
records.summary: Process-level organization of directed intracellular transport through cytoskeletal structures, motor activity, and regulated spatial routing.

records.description: Cellular Mechanisms of Immune Response denote the admissible process-level organization in which molecular recognition, intracellular signaling, and controlled effector actions are integrated into a coherent defensive regime at the cellular level. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing detection of non-self, altered-self, or damaged-self patterns, the amplification and routing of danger-related signals, and the execution of targeted defensive responses such as secretion of protective molecules, localized degradation of compromised components, or activation of programmed cell death. This process can operate within single cells and can also extend through immediate coordination with neighboring cells before the emergence of organism-scale immune systems. The arising establishes the regulated cellular defense architecture through which threat-sensitive recognition and response become structurally admissible.
records.name: Cellular Mechanisms of Immune Response

records.shortDescription: Process-level cellular defensive regime integrating recognition, signaling, and effector responses against internal and external threats.
records.summary: Process-level cellular defensive regime integrating recognition, signaling, and effector responses against internal and external threats.

records.description: Cellular Regulatory Networks denote the admissible pattern-level organization in which signaling pathways, gene-expression control, metabolic regulation, and feedback constraints become structurally integrated into a unified architecture governing cellular behavior as a whole. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a pattern because it consists in the stable relational configuration of interacting control nodes, feedback loops, feedforward motifs, conditional switches, and multi-timescale couplings rather than in a single bounded object or one ongoing process alone. Regulation at this level is distributed across network topology, coupling strength, and dynamical state, so cellular control is no longer attributable to isolated pathways or molecules. This arising establishes the global regulatory pattern through which the cell stabilizes internal conditions, switches between functional modes, maintains robustness under perturbation, and adapts to environmental and internal change.
records.name: Cellular Regulatory Networks
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level integration of signaling, gene expression, and metabolic control into a unified cellular regulatory architecture.
records.summary: Pattern-level integration of signaling, gene expression, and metabolic control into a unified cellular regulatory architecture.
